sentences.text: It is submitted that as per the prosecution story, incident took place on 23/03/2018.

sentences.text: It is pointed out that firstly the Ossification Report (Ex.P/13) is available on record which was proved by Dr. Shikhar Surana (PW-4).

sentences.text:
Dr. Shikhar Surana has categorically mentioned that age of the victim was above 16 years and below 17 years, therefore there was no occasion for the learned trial Court to have convicted the appellant under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC, inasmuch as before it was omitted w.e.f.

sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. Thus, when there is a medical evidence is available on record that victim was above 16 years of age, then there was no occasion to invoke the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 3 CRA-1606-2024 provisions of Section 376(2)(i) of IPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: This shows that learned trial Court Judge was not having proper legal knowledge as to the provision and its application.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 7. It is further submitted that despite there being an ossification report available on record, the trial Court considered age of the victim to be 13 years which is contrary to the prosecution case and documents available on record as were filed by the prosecution.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. It is further submitted that Section 4 of POCSO Act as it stood at the time of the incident, it was provided that 'Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
It is pointed out that this provision was amended w.e.f. 16/08/2019 and it was provided "(2) Whoever commits penetrative sexual assault on a child below 16 years of age shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than 20 years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of natural life of that person, and shall also be liable to fine.
9.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that this amended provision came into effect w.e.f. 16/08/2019 whereas offence is of the year 2018 and therefore, punishment will be as per the unamended provision, and this basic fact was ignored, over looked and grossly neglected by the learned trial Court Judge while handing over the punishment.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Thus, it is submitted that the trial Court Judge was not well versed in legal provisions and also on the aspect that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 4 Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185638148/
2 CRA-1606-2024 punishment was required to be handed over as was provided under the unamended provision which stood as on the date of commission of the offence and not of the subsequent dates.
10.

sentences.text: It is also pointed out that the FSL report though available on record at page 37 dated 19/04/2018 bearing No.BI/475/2018 issued by the Assistant Chemical Examiner, State of M.P. Regional Forensic Science Laboratory, Bhopal and addressed to Superintended of Police, Chhindwara, is available on record, but neither it was exhibited nor any question was put to the accused under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. despite the fact that learned trial Court has used that report in Para-24 of the impugned judgment.

sentences.text: Thus, it is pointed out that the learned trial Court was totally oblivious of appreciation of legal provisions, understanding of law and also its application.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 11. Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Government Advocate submits that even otherwise when Section 4 of POCSO Act remains unamended, if put to use prescribed life imprisonment, therefore sentence of 20 years cannot be faulted with.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 12. We are in total disagreement with the contention put-forth by Shri Manas Mani Verma, learned Public Prosecutor.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: The Senior Additional District Judge is suppose to understand law and apply it in its full force.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: We do not expect a Senior Additional District Judge given responsibility of acting as a Special Judge to be oblivious of legal provisions and understanding of the concerned Judge calls for a detailed scrutiny and investigation for which, we direct this file to be placed before Hon'ble the Chief Justice to take a call and decide as to whether the concerned Judge is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:49700 5 CRA-1606-2024 required to undergo refresher course or is entitled to continue in service as a Special Judge.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: 13. As far as merits are concerned, we are of the opinion that prosecution has proved the commission of offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, without dwelling on the aspect of conviction, we would like to record two findings, namely; conviction under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC is not made out and is hereby set aside.
sentences._hearing_file: Premlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 September, 2025.json

sentences.text: Secondly, the finding of the learned trial Court recorded in Para-38 that the age of the victim was 13 years, is not made out as contrary to the Ossification Report (Ex.P/13) of Expert which is proved by Dr. Shikhar Surana (PW-4), who categorically proved the age of the victim to be more than 16 years.

sentences.text: Therefore, under such facts and circumstances, while maintaining conviction under Sections 366, 506 Part-II of IPC r/w Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, we hold that appellant will undergo sentence of 10 years R.I. under Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, as it stood prior to the date of amendment i.e. 16/08/2019.

sentences.text: Other sentences shall remain intact.

sentences.text: All the sentences to run concurrently.

opennyai_summary.facts: The appellant/accused was prosecuted, convicted and sentenced regarding the incident dated 17.03.2012 in which appellant committed rape with the prosecutrix (PW-3) regarding which a crime no.129/2012 registered against the appellant at police station- Simrol, District- Indore (M.P.) under section under section 376 of the IPC.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Challenging the conviction as well as sentence this appeal has been preferred.
The appellant accused has been convicted and sentenced for minimum sentence and as per the Jail Report No.2796/Warrant/2025 dated 04.11.2025 of Jail Superintendent, Central Jail, Indore, the appellant/accused was released on 07.08.2024 after completing the sentence and depositing the fine amount and, accordingly, this appeal has no substance
